answer: Cross-Epoch Timing Continuity Rule. Each identity tracks inter-arrival gaps, retry spacing, and active-hour distribution. At each boundary, its next-epoch sample must match the prior horizon within tolerance; outliers are dropped. Batch-made sybils leave an echo of shared client timing and fail. Passing requires running each identity over epochs with separate paths, clocks, and jitter, costing compute and upkeep, not copying one timber template.
